newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: China informs U.N. of treaties affecting Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China informs U.N. of treaties affecting Hong Kong.

text.p: China informed the United Nations on Friday of actions it would take regarding 24 international treaties once the British colony of Hong Kong reverts to Beijing's sovereignty at the end of this month, the Chinese U.N. mission said.
The world body, as the depository of the treaties, was notified that 10 agreements to which China is currently a party would also apply to Hong Kong after the takeover.
These range from an international convention against the taking of hostages and a convention on narcotic drugs to a convention against genocide.
China said 14 other treaties to which Hong Kong, but not Beijing, is a party, would continue to apply to Hong Kong.
These include international conventions on such topics as the simplification of customs formalities, the temporary importation of commercial road vehicles and freedom of transit.
The United Nations is expected to receive similar notification soon from China concerning dozens of other international treaties that will apply, or continue to apply, to Hong Kong.
